items.claim: A broken access control finding is only real when a request issued as an identity that holds no permission for the resource or action still succeeds, so identity substitution on an otherwise-valid request is the test that separates the finding from normal behaviour.
items.body:
A broken access control finding is only real when a request issued as an identity that holds no permission for the resource or action still succeeds, so identity substitution on an otherwise-valid request is the test that separates the finding from normal behaviour.

HackTricks reference: broken access control and broken authentication (https://oreobiscuit.gitbook.io/introduction/bug-bounty-reports-and-articles/broken-access-control-and-broken-authentication.md)
items.disproof: If the same request replayed as a lower-privileged or unauthenticated identity is rejected or returns only the caller's own authorized data, the permission check is present and the access control claim fails.

sources.quote: This vulnerability arises when an application fails to enforce appropriate permissions, allowing users to access unauthorized resources or actions.
If authentication credentials were provided in the request, the server considers them insufficient to grant access. The client SHOULD NOT automatically repeat the request with the same credentials.
This is a business logic vulnerability that looks correct on the surface, as the code does verify the user has the right role. But verifying a role is not the same as verifying scope
